draft_content:
R.I.P. the 47-tab browser session for a single itinerary.

The era of coordinating multi-vendor quotes via fragmented WhatsApp threads and static spreadsheets is ending.

It is a slow, unglamorous death, but a necessary one.

I built Viato to address this specific operational bottleneck in TravelTech. The problem is not a lack of intent. It is the friction of manual data entry.

When a travel specialist juggles hotel confirmations, flight updates, and ground transport, the risk of a missed detail is high.

A single mis-typed date or a dropped supplier message can unravel an entire client trip.

We are betting on structure over speed. We are betting on centralizing customer preferences, supplier communications, and dynamic booking updates into one observable system.

This is not about replacing the human judgment of a boutique specialist. It is about removing the cognitive load of tracking who said what, and when.

The back-office work is dull. But it is the foundation of trust in the service industry.

How do you currently handle the risk of manual errors in high-stakes, multi-step service delivery?
